cards.stem: How is compound interest described for a savings account?
options: earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn
charges interest only on money borrowed from a bank
pays interest only on the first deposit made
cards.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.
cards.hint: Think about earning on both principal and previous interest.

cards.stem: What portion of earnings should go directly to savings after getting a steady job?
cards.quote: Once your teen has a steady job, help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.
cards.hint: Recall the savings program target for steady work.

cards.stem: What is the basic emergency saving goal mentioned as a good rule?
options: three months’ worth of living expenses
cards.quote: have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.
cards.hint: Consider how many months of expenses are recommended for emergencies.

cards.stem: In the example, what could saving $100 every year from age 14 grow to by the later age?
cards.quote: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they'd have about $23,000 at age 65.
cards.hint: Compare starting early with starting later in the example.
